Title: G-SYNC / VRR unnecessarily switches to frame doubling at around 60 FPS

I have noticed an issue with NVIDIA G-SYNC / VRR where the refresh rate appears to switch to a frame-doubling mode when the frame rate drops to approximately 60 FPS.

Instead of matching the refresh rate directly to the frame rate, the monitor appears to run at twice the frame rate (e.g. 60 FPS → 120 Hz, 55 FPS → 110 Hz). This results in unnecessary frame doubling and can potentially introduce stuttering, flickering, or inconsistent frame pacing.

This behavior seems to occur even when the monitor's actual VRR range should allow it to operate at these frame rates without frame doubling.

Expected behavior:
G-SYNC appears to activate frame doubling around 60 FPS, even though the monitor may still be capable of operating within its native VRR range at that frame rate.
Orbmu2k, the developer of NVIDIA Profile Inspector, has released a tool called NVIDIA G-SYNC Tweaks that allows users to modify the driver's LFC / frame-doubling behavior.
It would be great if NVIDIA could investigate this behavior and provide a proper driver-level fix or an official setting to control the LFC threshold and frame-doubling behavior.

Title: [BUG REPORT] Windows intermittently detects incorrect HDR peak brightness after startup (240 nits instead of 1038 nits)

Hello NVIDIA team,

I would like to report an intermittent HDR detection issue involving Windows 11, an RTX 5080, and an MSI QD-OLED monitor.

System configuration:

* GPU: KFA2 GeForce RTX 5080 Core Series
* CPU: AMD Ryzen 7 9800X3D
* Motherboard: MSI B850 Gaming Plus WiFi
* Monitor: MSI MAG 321UP QD-OLED X24
* Monitor firmware: FW.012
* Connection: DisplayPort 1.4a with DSC enabled
* Operating system: Windows 11 26H2 (upgraded from 23H2)
* NVIDIA driver: 621.24 WHQL

Issue description:

The issue can be fully resolved by either:
* True Black 500 mode: approximately 530 nits.
Once the correct brightness value is restored, it remains correct. The problem appears to occur during initial display/HDR initialization after Windows startup.
* Performed a clean NVIDIA driver removal using DDU in Safe Mode, including removal of existing/non-present monitor entries, followed by a clean installation of driver 621.24 WHQL.
* Restarted the NVIDIA graphics driver using Win + Ctrl + Shift + B. This did not resolve the issue.
* Tested another DisplayPort output on the GPU using the same cable. The issue persisted.
* Confirmed that the monitor’s OSD correctly displays the selected HDR mode even when Windows reports only 240 nits.
* Confirmed that no custom Windows HDR Calibration profiles are installed or being used.
This suggests that the incorrect 240-nit value may be caused by an issue during Windows/NVIDIA HDR capability initialization or the subsequent handling of EDID/DisplayID information over DisplayPort.
Could this issue be related to the NVIDIA driver failing to correctly initialize or refresh the monitor’s HDR capabilities during Windows startup?
In particular, I would appreciate investigation into the interaction between the NVIDIA driver, Windows Advanced Color/HDR initialization, and DisplayPort EDID/DisplayID or Hot Plug Detect (HPD) handling.

Subject: Persistent VRR (G-SYNC) flickering and pixel inversion with Frame Generation on 8-bit laptop display (Drivers 616.xx – 621.24)

System Configuration:
- Laptop: Lenovo LOQ (dGPU / MUX Switch mode enabled, Optimus disabled)
- GPU: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5060 Laptop GPU (100W)
- Display: Built-in 15.6" 144Hz IPS panel, 8-bit (6-bit + FRC), G-SYNC Compatible, Overdrive disabled
- Tested Drivers: Lenovo OEM 595.95 (Good) vs. Official NVIDIA 617.42, 621.14, 621.24 (Broken)
- Games Tested: Phantom Blade Zero and other DX12 titles with Frame Generation

Issue Description:
Ever since updating past the 595.95 OEM driver to the 616.xx–621.xx driver branch (including 617.42, 621.14, and the latest 621.24), there is severe screen flickering and subtle pixel inversion (shimmering/grid-like artifacts) whenever G-SYNC (VRR) is used together with Frame Generation (DLSS FG).
1. I tested an identical route in Phantom Blade Zero at 100% screen brightness with base FPS above 70+ and an FPS cap at 137 FPS (via RTSS Reflex mode).
2. On Lenovo OEM driver 595.95: Zero flickering occurs during the entire run.
3. On official drivers 617.42, 621.14, and 621.24: The screen flickers 6–7 times on the exact same route, and pixel inversion/shimmering never goes away.
4. This issue only happens in games with VRR + Frame Generation active (the desktop is completely normal). Disabling G-SYNC stops the flickering, which confirms it is a VRR / LFC threshold and 8-bit output/dithering regression introduced in the 616+ driver branch.
Since this built-in laptop panel is natively limited to 8-bit color depth, we cannot switch to 10-bit in the NVIDIA Control Panel as a workaround. Please investigate and fix the 8-bit dithering and LFC/VRR timing behavior with Frame Generation on laptop displays.
